title: Running & Building Your App
description: Start the dev server, create a production build, and understand the build output.

slides.title: Development Mode 🔧
slides.content:
# `npm run dev`

Inside your project folder, run:

```bash
npm run dev
```

* Starts a development server on `http://localhost:3000`
* Hot reload – changes are reflected instantly.
* Fast Refresh preserves component state.

quizData.question: What is the default port for the Next.js dev server?
quizData.explanation: Next.js dev server runs on port 3000 by default. You can change it with `-p` flag if needed.

slides.title: Production Build 📦
slides.content:
# `npm run build`

Creates an optimised production build:

* Compiles and minifies code.
* Pre‑renders pages (SSG).
* Outputs a `.next` folder with the production assets.

```bash
npm run build
npm start   # starts production server
```

slides.title: Build Output Example
slides.content: You'll see a summary of each page and its rendering strategy.
slides.codeSnippet:
Page                                       Size     First Load JS
┌ ○ /                                      5.1 kB         86.2 kB
├ ○ /about                                 2.3 kB         83.4 kB
└ ○ /contact                               2.5 kB         83.6 kB
+ First Load JS shared by all              81.1 kB
  ├ chunks/main-...js                      45.3 kB
  ├ chunks/webpack-...js                   3.4 kB
  └ other shared chunks                    32.4 kB

○  (Static)  automatically rendered as static HTML

quizData.question: What does the ○ symbol next to a page mean in the build output?

options.text: It was statically generated at build time (SSG)

quizData.explanation: A hollow circle (○) indicates a page that was statically generated. It does not require a server at runtime.
